Theorem 23: ! ! ! $A_n T_n = B_n + K_n$ ! ! ! ! ! ! $(B_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ ! ! ! ! ! !…
nodes.statement: Assume that 21 is satisfied. Then, there exist sequences $(B_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}, (K_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$, $B_n \in L(\mathbb{X}_n)$, $K_n \in L(\mathbb{X}_n)$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $A_n T_n = B_n + K_n$ with $(B_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ being uniformly bounded. $(B_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is \hyperlink{stable}{stable}, $(K_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is \hyperlink{compactop}{compact}~and there exists a bijective operator $B \in L(\mathbb{X}_n)$ such that $B_n$ \hyperlink{approximate}{approximates}~$B$.

nodes.name: Theorem 24: $(A_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ $(\mathbf{u}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ $\mathbf{u}$
nodes.statement: Assume that 21 holds. For $\mathbf{f} \in \mathbf{L}^2$, let $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{X}$ be the solution to (8). Then, there exists an index $n_0 > 0$ such that for all $n > n_0$ the problem (17) has a unique solution $\mathbf{u}_n \in \mathbb{X}_n$ and $\lim_{n \to \infty} d_n(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{u}_n) = 0$.
